questions.question: Which blood group has no antibody?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AB**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Type AB blood is rare** it’s found in **less than 5% **of the population.
 
• And it is the **'newest' of the blood types.**
 
• Until ten or twelve centuries ago, there was little to no Type AB blood type.
 
• That is because type AB results from the intermingling of Type A with Type B.
 
• Type AB **has both A and B antigens**, **but no antibodies.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the years 1900–1902, K. Landsteiner divided human blood into four groups — A, B, AB, and O.
 
• Rh factor is a type of blood antigen discovered in 1940 by Landsteiner and A.K. s. was done by Veneer.
 
• Each person has a blood type (O, A, B, or AB). Everyone also has an Rh factor (positive or negative).
 
• The Rh factor is a protein on the covering of the red blood cells.
 
• If the Rh factor protein is on the cells, the person is Rh-positive.
 
• If there’s no Rh factor protein, the person is Rh-negative.

questions.question: If the object is placed beyond the center of curvature (C) in front of a concave mirror, the image formed will be ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**real, inverted and diminished**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed beyond the center of curvature (C) in front of a concave mirror, the image formed is **real and inverted**.
 
• The image size is **diminished** compared to the actual object.
 
• The image is formed between the **focus (F)** and the **center of curvature (C)**.
 
• This property of concave mirrors is utilized in various optical instruments like telescopes and shaving mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:** A spherical mirror that curves inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• **Focal Point (F):** The point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to converge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• **Center of Curvature (C):** The center of the sphere from which the concave mirror is a part.
 
• **Real Image:** An image that can be projected onto a screen because light rays actually converge at the image location.
 
• **Inverted Image:** An image that is upside down relative to the object.
 
• Concave mirrors are widely used in **headlights** of vehicles, **optical instruments**, and in **solar furnaces** for their ability to focus light.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is evolved when ethanol reacts with sodium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen gas** is evolved when ethanol reacts with sodium.
 
• The reaction between ethanol and sodium can be represented by the chemical equation: **2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂**.
 
• In this reaction, ethanol (C₂H₅OH) reacts with sodium (Na) to form sodium ethoxide (C₂H₅ONa) and hydrogen gas (H₂).
 
• This is a typical reaction of alcohols with reactive metals like sodium, where hydrogen gas is released as a byproduct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ethanol** (C₂H₅OH) is a type of alcohol commonly found in alcoholic beverages and also used as a solvent and in chemical synthesis.
 
• The reaction of ethanol with sodium is an example of a **single displacement reaction**, where one element (hydrogen) in a compound (ethanol) is replaced by another element (sodium).
 
• Sodium ethoxide (C₂H₅ONa) formed in the reaction is a strong base and is often used in organic synthesis.
 
• Hydrogen gas (H₂) is a colorless, odorless gas that is highly flammable and is used in various industrial processes, including the production of ammonia and hydrogenation of fats and oils.

questions.question: While standing on Earth, suppose your weight has a value of 100 Newtons. If the Earth shrinks to half its diameter without any change in mass, then your new weight on the surface of the shrunken Earth, in Newtons, is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**400.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Weight of the body (W1) = mg;
 
• The surface of the earth with radius R. (Given 100 Newtons)
 
• Acceleration due to gravity on earth (g) = G.M/R²,
 
 
• G is gravitation constant, (M) is mass of earth and R is the initial radius of the earth.
 
 
 
• Now Final radius =R/2;
 
• New acceleration due to gravity on earth (g2) = (G.M)/(R/2)² = 4(G.M/R²) = 4g
 
• So new weight of Body (W2) = m. g2 = 4(m.g) [as mass of body is constant]
 
• **From above,**
 
 
• **W2 = 4* W1 =4*100 = 400 Newtons**. **Hence option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: Which of these is NOT biodegradable?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Plastic cups**.

__Explanation:__

 
• Biodegradability refers to the ability of a material to decompose naturally with the help of microorganisms, such as bacteria and fungi, without harming the environment.
 
• Non-biodegradable materials do not decompose easily and can persist in the environment for hundreds of years, leading to pollution and other ecological issues.
 
 
• **Plastic Cups:** Plastic cups are made from synthetic polymers derived from petrochemicals, such as polyethylene or polystyrene. These materials are non-biodegradable because microorganisms cannot break them down into simpler substances. As a result, plastic waste accumulates in the environment, causing pollution, harming wildlife, and contributing to microplastic contamination. This is why plastic cups are considered non-biodegradable.
 
• **Kulhads:** Kulhads are traditional Indian cups made from clay. They are biodegradable because clay is a natural material, and microorganisms can break it down over time. Additionally, kulhads are eco-friendly as they do not release harmful chemicals into the environment during decomposition.
 
• **Disposable Paper Cups:** Disposable paper cups are made primarily from paper, which is biodegradable.
 
• **Vegetable Peels:** Vegetable peels are organic waste derived from plants. They are completely biodegradable and decompose quickly with the help of microorganisms. When composted, vegetable peels can enrich the soil and support plant growth, making them an eco-friendly option.

questions.question: The image formed by a convex mirror is always _________.

options.text: inverted and of same size as the object
erect and of same size as the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**erect and diminished**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex mirror** is a diverging mirror that curves outward. It reflects light rays outward, meaning they appear to originate from a point behind the mirror.
 
• The image formed by a convex mirror is always **virtual**, as the reflected rays never actually meet but seem to converge when extended backward. *Hence, the image is not real.*
 
• The image formed is always **erect** because it appears upright relative to the object. This is a characteristic of convex mirrors.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce a **diminished** image, meaning the image size is smaller than the actual object size. This occurs regardless of the object's distance from the mirror.
 
• The position of the image is always behind the mirror, and it appears closer to the mirror as the object moves farther away.
 
• Convex mirrors are often used in vehicles as **rearview mirrors** because they provide a wider field of view, allowing drivers to see more area behind them.
 
• The other options are incorrect as a convex mirror *cannot produce an inverted image* and does not form an image of the same size as the object. The image is always diminished and upright. *Hence, the correct answer is erect and diminished.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Convex Mirrors:**

 
 
• **Convex mirrors** are diverging mirrors that reflect light outward. They are designed to provide a wide field of view, making them ideal for safety and surveillance purposes.
 
• The image formed by a convex mirror is always **virtual, erect, and diminished**. These characteristics are independent of the object's distance from the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors are widely used as **rearview mirrors** in vehicles because they give a wider field of view and help drivers detect traffic from behind.
 
• They are also used in **security and surveillance** in shops, parking lots, and blind corners to monitor activities across a wide area.
 
 
 
• **Principles of Image Formation:**
 
 
• The laws of reflection govern the behavior of light rays on convex mirrors. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
 
• In convex mirrors, the reflected rays diverge, and the image appears to form behind the mirror when the rays are extended backward.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Concave Mirrors:**

 
 
• Unlike convex mirrors, **concave mirrors** can form both real and virtual images. The image can be magnified, inverted, or diminished depending on the object's position relative to the mirror's focal point.
 
• Convex mirrors are preferred for applications requiring a wide field of view, while concave mirrors are used in applications like telescopes, headlights, and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Real-Life Examples:**
 
 
• A common example of a convex mirror is the **side-view mirror** in cars. It often comes with the warning, "Objects in the mirror are closer than they appear," due to the diminished size of the image.
 
• Convex mirrors are also used in **road safety** at blind turns or intersections to provide visibility and reduce accidents.

questions.question: The ability of the eyes lens to adjust its focal length is called ________.
questions.solution:
__**Concept-**__

The ability of the eye lens to modify its focal length is referred to as **accommodation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f026e52dafa76280cf25085bb402ca7afe547d0066049fae3a34e00b8f2ec5c2.png] 

__
 
• The **action of ciliary muscles** is responsible for the entire process.
 
• The focal length of the eye lens is altered.
 
• For a crisp picture of adjacent objects, the ciliary muscles strain and contract the lens, whereas, for distant objects, it relaxes and returns to its flatter shape.
 
• The "dioptre" is a unit of lens power.
 
• The **maximum variation or change in its power for focusing on nearby as well as far things is known as power of accommodation**.
 
• The power accommodation for a normal individual is roughly 4 dioptres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **reciprocal of the focal length is called power of lens. **Dioptres are a unit of measurement for lens power (D). Because convergent (convex) lenses have positive focal lengths, their power values are also positive. Diverging (concave) lenses have negative focal lengths, hence their power values are negative.
 
• The **bending of light beams as they move through one object to another is known as refraction**. Light rays are bent (refracted) by the cornea and lens to focus on the retina. When the shape of the eye changes, the way light rays bend and focus changes as well, which can result in hazy vision.
 
• **When a ray of light strikes a polished, smooth, or glossy item, the light from that object reflects back to our eyes, which is known as "Reflection" or "Reflection of Light**."This phenomenon is what allows us to see the world through our eyes.

questions.question: Where is the minimum weight of a body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**At the equator.**__

__
 
• **The minimum weight of a body is at the equator.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Due to the effect of gravity, the weight of the body is minimum at the equator.
 
• As the distance of the equator from the center of the earth is maximum, so the force of attraction is lowest on the body at the equator. Hence the weight of a body is minimum at the equator.
 
• **Gravity:**
 
 
• The acceleration due to gravity is the rate of increase of velocity of a body falling freely towards the earth.
 
• It is represented by g= {GM_e over R_e²}
 
 
 
• 
 
where **Me is the mass of the earth** and **Re is the radius of the earth.**

 
 
• The value of g at the surface of the earth is **9**.8 m/s².
 
• Variation in g:
 
 
• **The value of g decreases with height or depth from the earth’s surface.**
 
• g is **maximum at poles**. Hence, it will be maximum at the Camp in Antarctica
 
• g is **minimum at the equator.**
 
• g **decreases due to the rotation of the earth**.
 
• g decreases if the angular speed of earth increases and increases if the angular speed of earth decreases

Time (t) = 2 s

Power (P) =?

**Power = 500 W. **So option 3 is correct.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to reproduction in plants?

1. In asexual reproduction plants produce seeds identical to the parent.

2. In sexual reproduction parents and progeny have the same genetic makeup.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither 1 nor 2.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Reproduction in Plants:**

 
• The **production of new individuals from their parents** is known as Reproduction.
 
• There are **different modes of reproduction** in plants:
 
 
• Asexual Reproduction
 
• Sexual Reproduction
 
 

**Asexual Reproduction:**

 
• In asexual reproduction, new plants are obtained **without the production of seeds. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The new plants are **exact copies of the parent plant,** as they are produced from a** single parent.**
 
• It **does not include the fusion **of male and female gametes.
 
• It results in **offspring that are genetically identical** to their parents.
 
• **Examples: **
 
 
• **​**Budding, Fragmentation, Vegetative Propagation.
 
 

**Sexual Reproduction:**

 
• In sexual reproduction,** new plants are obtained from seeds.**
 
• Sexual reproduction** necessitates the genetic material of two parents.**
 
• Male and female sex cells, **known as gametes, **exist in parent plants.
 
• The **genetic material from the male and female gametes mixes **is referred to as **fertilisation**.
 
• As a result, neither of the parents and offspring are genetically similar. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Seeds** are the result of sexual reproduction.
 
• **Pollination** is the process through which flowering plants **reproduce sexually.**
